meta.title: Towing and learner driving
meta.summary: You will learn how to tow a broken-down car correctly, when towing is prohibited, and what rules apply to learner driving on the roads.

lesson.h: Three ways to tow a vehicle
p: A broken-down vehicle can be towed in three ways ⟦19⟧:
list: using a flexible coupling, that is a tow rope;
using a rigid coupling, that is a rigid tow bar;
by the method of partial lifting: the front part of the towed vehicle is raised on a special support device, or it is partially loaded onto the platform of the towing vehicle.
lesson.tip: The more rigid the link between the vehicles, the lower the risk of collision when braking. That is why, in difficult conditions, the Rules allow only a rigid tow bar or partial lifting.

lesson.h: Who must be in the towed vehicle
p: When towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar, there must be a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle. The driver steers and brakes so as not to run into the towing vehicle ⟦20⟧.
Towing without a driver is allowed only on a rigid tow bar whose design ensures that, when driving in a straight line, the towed vehicle follows exactly the same path as the towing vehicle ⟦21⟧.
A tow rope that is too short leaves the driver of the towed vehicle no time to brake. One that is too long makes the vehicle start to sway from side to side, making it harder to control.
list: Tow rope: from 4 to 6 metres ⟦22⟧.
Rigid tow bar: no more than 4 metres ⟦23⟧.

p: The Rules set no other restrictions on passengers: for example, you may ride inside the towing car, or in a car being towed on a rope, next to the driver.
list: On a tow rope or rigid tow bar: in a towed bus or trolleybus, and in the load body of a towed truck ⟦24⟧.
When the front is raised or by partial lifting: in the cab and load body of the towed vehicle, and in the load body of the towing vehicle ⟦25⟧.
The steering does not work. Exception: raising the front or partial lifting ⟦26⟧.
Towing two or more vehicles at once ⟦27⟧.

The braking system does not work and the actual mass of the towed vehicle is more than half the actual mass of the towing vehicle. If it is less, towing is allowed only on a rigid tow bar or by partial lifting ⟦28⟧.
By a motorcycle without a sidecar, and towing such a motorcycle itself ⟦29⟧.
On a tow rope in black ice conditions ⟦30⟧.
Towing a moped, and towing by a moped. Exception: a trailer designed for use with a moped ⟦31⟧.
lesson.tip: Black ice plus a tow rope - prohibited. You need a rigid tow bar or partial lifting.

list: When towing motor vehicles, the speed must not exceed 50 km/h regardless of the towing method, even if the signs allow more ⟦32⟧. For comparison: a passenger car with a trailer may travel at up to 70-90 km/h outside a built-up area, depending on the road ⟦33⟧.
The towed motor vehicle has its hazard warning lights switched on ⟦34⟧.
If there are no hazard warning lights or they do not work, a warning triangle is fixed to the rear of the towed vehicle ⟦35⟧.
During hours of darkness and in poor visibility, the towed vehicle must have its position lamps on ⟦36⟧.
The tow rope is marked with at least two flags or panels measuring 200 × 200 mm, with alternating red and white diagonal stripes and a retroreflective surface (Basic Provisions, para. 12).

p: The first driving skills are learned only in an enclosed area or at a test ground ⟦37⟧. There is no flow of vehicles and pedestrians there, so a beginner's mistake will not harm anyone.
A training vehicle goes out onto the road only once the learner already has basic skills, the instructor is present, and there are no passengers in the vehicle ⟦38⟧.

lesson.h: Who may teach and what documents are needed
list: The instructor must carry a qualification certificate and a driving licence of the category they are teaching ⟦39⟧.
The learner must carry an identity document and a medical certificate confirming no contraindications to driving a vehicle ⟦40⟧.
On public roads, teaching takes place only along routes agreed with the authorised body, and in the presence of a driving instructor ⟦41⟧.
lesson.tip: A friend or relative who holds a driving licence but has no qualification certificate cannot teach you to drive on the road.

lesson.h: Where learner driving is prohibited and who is responsible for it
list: On motorways (sign 5.1) and roads with sign 5.3 “Road for motor vehicles” ⟦42⟧.
In residential zones (sign 5.38) and in residential courtyards ⟦43⟧.
During the training process, the driving instructor is treated as the driver ⟦44⟧.
It is prohibited to hand over control to a person without a driving licence; the exception is a person learning to drive ⟦45⟧.
lesson.tip: Practise parking and U-turns at a test ground, not in the yard outside your home.

p: A vehicle used for training is fitted out to meet the requirements of para. 6 of the Basic Provisions on Admitting Vehicles to Operation ⟦46⟧. A training organisation's vehicle is fitted with additional clutch and brake pedals so that the instructor can intervene at a dangerous moment, and the words “Learner vehicle” are painted on its sides and rear in the state language.

The “Learner vehicle” identification sign is fitted at the front and rear: a white equilateral triangle, apex up, with a red border and a black letter U. The side of the triangle must be at least 200 mm. On a passenger car, a double-sided sign on the roof is allowed (para. 9 of the Basic Provisions).

keyFacts: Ways to tow a vehicle: tow rope, rigid tow bar, partial lifting or raising the front ⟦1⟧.
On a tow rope or rigid tow bar, a driver is needed at the wheel of the towed vehicle ⟦2⟧.
Tow rope: 4-6 m between the vehicles; rigid tow bar: no more than 4 m ⟦3⟧.
Speed when towing: no more than 50 km/h with any method ⟦4⟧.
If the steering does not work, towing is allowed only by raising the front or partial lifting ⟦5⟧.
Towing on a tow rope is prohibited in black ice conditions; a rigid tow bar is allowed ⟦6⟧.
Brakes not working: if the mass of the towed vehicle is more than half the mass of the towing vehicle - not allowed; if less - only a rigid tow bar or partial lifting ⟦7⟧.
You must not tow two or more vehicles at once, tow with a motorcycle without a sidecar or tow such a motorcycle, or tow a moped or tow with a moped, except for a trailer designed for a moped ⟦8⟧.
The towed vehicle has its hazard warning lights switched on, and if it has none, a warning triangle is fixed to its rear ⟦9⟧.
Initial training takes place in an enclosed area or at a test ground; on the road, only with an instructor, once basic skills are in place, and without passengers ⟦10⟧.
Training on public roads follows agreed routes and takes place in the presence of a driving instructor ⟦11⟧.
Learner driving is prohibited on motorways, in residential zones and in yards ⟦12⟧.
mistakes: “The longer the rope, the safer.” The distance between the vehicles on a tow rope must be from 4 to 6 m ⟦13⟧.
Towing a vehicle with failed steering on a rope. Such a vehicle can only be towed by raising the front or by partial lifting ⟦14⟧.
Towing on a rope in black ice, “just slowly.” This is prohibited: you need a rigid tow bar or partial lifting ⟦15⟧.
Driving at normal speed while towing. The limit is 50 km/h ⟦16⟧.
Assuming that any experienced driver can teach someone to drive. You need a qualification certificate, an agreed route and a driving instructor ⟦17⟧.
Practising with a learner in a yard or on a motorway. Learner driving is prohibited there ⟦18⟧.

questions.q: You are about to tow a friend's car on a rope 9 metres long. What should you do?
options: You can drive: a long rope is safer than a short one
Shorten the rope so that there is 4-6 m between the vehicles
Shorten the rope to 2 m so that the vehicle does not swerve
You can drive if you switch on the hazard warning lights
questions.explain: When towing on a tow rope, the distance between the towing and towed vehicles must be within 4-6 m. On a rigid tow bar, it must be no more than 4 m.

questions.q: May you tow a passenger car on a tow rope if there is no one at its wheel?
options: Yes, if you drive at a speed of no more than 50 km/h
Yes, if the distance between the vehicles is no more than 4 metres
No, there must be a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle
questions.explain: Towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar is allowed only when there is a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle. Without a driver, it is allowed only on a special rigid tow bar that keeps the vehicle on the towing vehicle's path.

questions.q: You are towing a truck on a rigid tow bar. Which statement is correct?
options: Passengers are not allowed in the load body of the towed truck
Passengers may ride in the load body if the sides are closed
A driver is never needed in the towed truck on a rigid tow bar
Passengers may ride in the load body if the speed is no more than 50 km/h
questions.explain: When towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar, passengers are not allowed in a towed bus (trolleybus) or in the load body of a towed truck. A driver is needed at the wheel of the towed vehicle, except when the design of the rigid tow bar keeps the vehicle exactly on the towing vehicle's path ⟦47⟧.

questions.q: There is black ice outside. You only have a tow rope. May you use it to tow a broken-down car?
options: Yes, if you drive no faster than 30 km/h
Yes, if the rope is no longer than 4 metres
Yes, if both vehicles have their hazard warning lights switched on
No: towing on a rope is prohibited in black ice conditions
questions.explain: Towing on a tow rope is prohibited in black ice conditions. In such conditions, you may use a rigid tow bar or partial lifting.

questions.q: The steering of a car has failed. How may it be towed?
options: On a tow rope with a driver at the wheel
On a rigid tow bar no more than 4 m long
Only by raising the front or by partial lifting
By any method, if the speed does not exceed 50 km/h
questions.explain: It is prohibited to tow a vehicle with non-functioning steering. Only towing by raising the front or by partial lifting is allowed.

questions.q: The brakes are not working on a passenger car with an actual mass of 1500 kg. It is to be towed by another passenger car with an actual mass of 1800 kg. How can this be done?
options: On a tow rope
It cannot be done; such towing is prohibited
On a rigid tow bar
On any coupling, if you drive no faster than 50 km/h
questions.explain: Half of 1800 kg is 900 kg, and the towed vehicle weighs 1500 kg. Towing a vehicle with a non-functioning braking system is prohibited if its actual mass is more than half the actual mass of the towing vehicle. If the mass is less, only a rigid tow bar or partial lifting is allowed.

questions.q: You are about to tow a friend's broken-down car on a rope. An acquaintance of yours who has no driving licence wants to sit at its wheel. May you drive like this?
options: Yes: the engine of the towed car is not running
No: the towed vehicle needs a licensed driver
Yes, if the speed does not exceed 50 km/h
Yes, if he only steers and brakes
questions.explain: When towing on a rope, there must be a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle ⟦48⟧, that is, a person who is driving it ⟦49⟧. You may not drive a vehicle without a driving licence ⟦50⟧, and handing over control to such a person is also prohibited ⟦51⟧.

questions.q: Your car is being towed on a rope. Its hazard warning lights are not working. What should be done?
options: Nothing: hazard warning lights are needed only on the towing vehicle
Switch on the main-beam headlights
Switch on the rear fog lamp
Fix a warning triangle to the rear
questions.explain: The towed motor vehicle has its hazard warning lights switched on ⟦52⟧. If it has none, or they are faulty, a warning triangle is fixed to the rear of the towed vehicle.

questions.q: Your friend, an experienced driver with a category B licence, offers to teach you to drive using his car on city streets. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if your friend has more than 3 years of driving experience and there are no passengers in the car
Yes, if you put the “Learner vehicle” sign on the car
No: only a driving instructor may teach on the road
Yes, if you only drive on streets with light traffic
questions.explain: The instructor must have a qualification certificate and a licence of the required category ⟦53⟧. Training on public roads takes place only along routes agreed with the authorised body, and in the presence of a driving instructor ⟦54⟧.

questions.q: Learner driving is taking place in the city, with a driving instructor next to you. An acquaintance asks for a lift on your way. May you take him in the car?
options: No, learner driving allows no passengers
Yes, if he sits in the back seat of the car
Yes, if he already has a driving licence
questions.explain: Learner driving on the roads is allowed only with an instructor present, once the learner has basic skills, and with no passengers in the vehicle.

questions.q: What methods of towing motor vehicles do the Rules provide for?
options: Only on a rope or a rigid bar, with a driver
On a coupling, by raising the front, or by partial lifting
Only on a rigid tow bar and on a recovery truck's platform
By any method the towed vehicle can withstand
questions.explain: Towing is carried out using a coupling (flexible or rigid), or by raising the front part of the vehicle on a special support device of the towing vehicle, or by partial lifting onto its platform ⟦55⟧.

questions.q: What does towing by the method of partial lifting mean?
options: The towed vehicle is partly loaded onto the towing vehicle's platform
The towed vehicle is fully loaded into the load body of a truck
The towed vehicle is partly unloaded to make it lighter
Towing two vehicles at once on one coupling
questions.explain: With partial lifting, the towed vehicle is partly loaded onto the platform of the towing vehicle. A similar method is raising the front part on a special support device of the towing vehicle ⟦56⟧.

questions.q: In which case may a car be towed on a rigid tow bar without a driver at the wheel?
options: If the towing speed is no more than 20 km/h
If the towed car is lighter than the towing car
In no case: a driver is always needed
If the tow bar keeps it on the towing vehicle's path
questions.explain: Towing on a rigid tow bar or a tow rope is done only with a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle. There is one exception: the design of the rigid tow bar ensures that the towed vehicle follows the towing vehicle's path when driving in a straight line ⟦57⟧.

questions.q: Your car is being towed on a rigid tow bar, and the distance between the vehicles is 5 m. Is this allowed?
options: Yes: on a rigid tow bar, 4 to 6 m is allowed
Yes, if the speed is no more than 50 km/h
No: on a rigid tow bar the distance must be no more than 4 m
No: on a rigid tow bar the distance must be at least 6 m
questions.explain: Here there are 5 m between the vehicles. On a rigid tow bar, the distance between the towing and towed vehicles must be no more than 4 m, while 4-6 m is the norm for a tow rope ⟦58⟧.

questions.q: Your car is being towed on a rope, and the distance between the vehicles is about 3 m. Is this allowed?
options: Yes: the shorter the rope, the safer the towing
Yes, if the rope is marked with flags or panels
Yes, if the towing speed is no more than 30 km/h
No: on a tow rope you need 4 to 6 m
questions.explain: On a rope at 3 m, the driver of the towed vehicle will not have time to react if the towing vehicle brakes sharply. On a tow rope, the distance between the vehicles must be within 4-6 m ⟦59⟧.

questions.q: According to the Basic Provisions, how is the flexible connecting link (rope) marked when towing?
options: With at least two red-and-white flags or panels
With one red flag fixed in the middle of the rope
With yellow reflective tape along the whole length of the rope
Not at all: the hazard warning lights on the vehicle are enough
questions.explain: Warning devices for flexible connecting links are flags or panels measuring 200 × 200 mm, with alternating red and white diagonal stripes 50 mm wide and a retroreflective surface. At least two such devices are fitted to the flexible link (Basic Provisions, para. 12).

questions.q: A broken-down bus is being towed on a rigid tow bar. May passengers stay inside it?
options: Yes, if the towing speed is no more than 50 km/h
No: passengers are not allowed in a towed bus
Yes, if there are no more than eight of them
Yes, if there is a driver at the wheel of the bus
questions.explain: When towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar, passengers are not allowed in a towed bus (trolleybus) or in the load body of a towed truck ⟦60⟧. A driver is still needed at the wheel of the bus ⟦61⟧.

questions.q: A broken-down truck is being towed by the method of partial lifting. May a passenger ride in the cab of this truck?
options: Yes, if he is wearing a seat belt
Yes, if the towing speed is no more than 30 km/h
No: riding in the cab of a towed vehicle is prohibited
Yes, but only during daylight hours
questions.explain: The towed truck stands at an angle on the platform, and it is dangerous to be in the cab. When towing by raising the front or by partial lifting, passengers are not allowed in the cab or load body of the towed vehicle, or in the load body of the towing vehicle ⟦62⟧.

questions.q: Where are passengers not allowed to be when towing by raising the front or by partial lifting?
options: Only inside or in the cab of the towing vehicle
In the towed vehicle and the towing vehicle's load body
Only in the load body of the towed truck
Nowhere, if the towing speed is no more than 50 km/h
questions.explain: When raising the front or using partial lifting, passengers are not allowed in the cab or load body of the towed vehicle, or in the load body of the towing vehicle ⟦63⟧. Riding in the cab of the towing vehicle is allowed.

questions.q: A truck is towing two cars at once on ropes, as shown in the diagram. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if each rope is 4-6 m long
Yes, if the speed is no more than 30 km/h
Yes, if there is a driver at the wheel of each car
No: towing two or more vehicles at once is prohibited
questions.explain: In the diagram, the truck is pulling a blue car, and that car is pulling yours. Towing two or more vehicles is prohibited ⟦64⟧: such a “train” is hard to steer and brake.

questions.q: The brakes are not working on your car, which has an actual mass of 1200 kg. You will be towed by a truck with an actual mass of 4000 kg. How can this be done?
options: Only on a rigid tow bar or by the method of partial lifting
By any method, including on a rope
It cannot be done: towing with faulty brakes is not allowed
Only on a rope 4-6 m long
questions.explain: Half the mass of the truck is 2000 kg, and your car weighs 1200 kg, that is, less. In that case, towing a vehicle with a non-functioning braking system is allowed, but only on a rigid tow bar or by the method of partial lifting ⟦65⟧.

questions.q: You are riding a motorcycle without a sidecar, and another motorcycle like it is about to tow you on a rope. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if the rope is 4 to 6 m long
Yes, if you use a rigid tow bar
No: such towing is prohibited
Yes, if both riders are wearing helmets
questions.explain: A two-wheeled motorcycle easily loses balance when a rope jerks it. That is why towing by a motorcycle without a sidecar, and towing of such a motorcycle, is prohibited ⟦66⟧.

questions.q: May a motorcycle without a sidecar be towed by a passenger car?
options: Yes, on a rope 4 to 6 m long
Yes, on a rigid tow bar no longer than 4 m
No, such a motorcycle may not be towed
Yes, if the rider is sitting at the handlebars
questions.explain: Not only is towing by a motorcycle without a sidecar prohibited, but so is towing such a motorcycle itself, whatever is used to pull it ⟦67⟧. A broken-down motorcycle is carried as cargo.

questions.q: There is black ice on the road. You have a rigid tow bar. May you use it to tow a broken-down car?
options: No: towing is prohibited by any method in black ice conditions
Yes: in black ice conditions, only a tow rope is prohibited
Only by the method of partial lifting
Yes, but only during daylight hours
questions.explain: The prohibition applies only to a tow rope: on black ice, a vehicle towed on a rope may catch up with and hit the towing vehicle ⟦68⟧. A rigid tow bar keeps the distance fixed, so towing on it is allowed, at no more than 50 km/h ⟦69⟧.

questions.q: Which of these do the Rules allow to be towed by a moped?
options: Another broken-down moped on a rope 4-6 m long
A bicycle on a rigid tow bar up to 4 m long
Any vehicle at least twice as light as the moped
Only a trailer designed for a moped
questions.explain: Towing mopeds, and towing by mopeds, is prohibited. There is one exception: a moped may tow a trailer designed for use with a moped ⟦70⟧.

questions.q: Your car is being towed on a rigid tow bar, and the distance between the vehicles is 3 m. Is this allowed?
options: Yes: on a rigid tow bar, no more than 4 m is allowed
No: there must be 4 to 6 m between the vehicles
No: on a rigid tow bar you need at least 5 m
Yes, but only at a speed of no more than 30 km/h
questions.explain: Here there are 3 m between the vehicles. On a rigid tow bar, the distance must be no more than 4 m, so 3 m is fine, while the 4-6 m norm applies to a tow rope ⟦71⟧.

questions.q: A truck is towing your car on a rope marked with flags. There is 5 m between the vehicles, you are at the wheel, your car's hazard warning lights are on, and the road is dry. What has been broken here?
options: The rope is too short
Hazard warning lights are not needed on the towed vehicle
A truck is not allowed to tow a passenger car
Nothing has been broken
questions.explain: All the conditions are met: there is a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle ⟦72⟧, the distance on the tow rope is within 4-6 m ⟦73⟧, the rope is marked (Basic Provisions, para. 12), the towed vehicle has its hazard warning lights on ⟦74⟧, and there is no black ice ⟦75⟧. All that is left is not to exceed 50 km/h ⟦76⟧.

questions.q: Your broken-down car is being towed on a rope, and you are at the wheel. May your friend ride next to you in the front seat?
options: No: there must be no passengers in a towed vehicle
Yes, but only in the back seat, not next to you
Yes: there is no such prohibition for a passenger car
No, if the towing rope is longer than 4 m
questions.explain: When towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar, the Rules ban passengers only in a towed bus (trolleybus) and in the load body of a towed truck ⟦77⟧. There is no such ban for the inside of a towed passenger car.

questions.q: Where is initial driver training carried out?
options: On quiet city streets
On country roads with light traffic
In enclosed areas or at test grounds
In the yards of residential buildings
questions.explain: Initial driver training is carried out in enclosed areas or at test grounds ⟦78⟧: there is no flow of vehicles and pedestrians there. Learner driving is prohibited altogether in yards and residential zones ⟦79⟧.

questions.q: A driving-school student has sat at the wheel for the first time. May he go straight out onto a city street if a driving instructor is next to him?
options: Yes, if a driving instructor is sitting next to him
No: basic skills in an enclosed area are needed first
Yes, if the car is fitted with additional pedals
Yes, if you choose a street with no traffic jams at the moment
questions.explain: Skills are first acquired in an enclosed area or at a test ground ⟦80⟧. Learner driving on the roads is allowed only with an instructor, once the learner has basic skills, and without passengers ⟦81⟧.

questions.q: What documents must a learner carry during learner driving?
options: A driving licence and a medical certificate
A qualification certificate and a contract with the driving school
Only a contract with the driving school; nothing else is needed
An identity document and a medical certificate
questions.explain: The learner carries an identity document and a medical certificate confirming no contraindications to driving a vehicle. A qualification certificate and a licence of the required category are the instructor's documents ⟦82⟧.

questions.q: A driving instructor has a qualification certificate, but only a category B driving licence. May he conduct learner driving in a category C truck?
options: No: he needs the category he is teaching
Yes, if the truck is fitted out as a training vehicle
Yes, if the route is agreed with the authorised body
Yes, if the student already drives a passenger car
questions.explain: The instructor carries a qualification certificate and a driving licence entitling him to drive a vehicle of the category he is teaching ⟦83⟧. A category B licence is not enough for a category C truck.

questions.q: What must a training organisation's car be fitted with for driver training?
options: Additional clutch and brake pedals and the “Learner vehicle” sign
A second steering wheel and an additional interior mirror for the instructor
A dashcam and additional side mirrors
An amber beacon and the “Learner vehicle” sign
questions.explain: A training vehicle is fitted out under para. 6 of the Basic Provisions ⟦84⟧: additional clutch and brake pedals, the “Learner vehicle” identification sign, and the words “Learner vehicle” in the state language on the sides and rear.

questions.q: What does the “Learner vehicle” identification sign look like?
options: A yellow circle with a black border and a black letter U
A blue square with a white border and a white letter U
A white triangle with a red border and a black letter U
A red triangle with a white border and a white letter U
questions.explain: The “Learner vehicle” sign is a white equilateral triangle, apex up, with a red border, inside which is a black letter U. The side must be at least 200 mm, and the width of the border is 1/10 of the side (Basic Provisions, para. 9).

questions.q: Where is the “Learner vehicle” identification sign fitted on a passenger car?
options: Only at the rear, in the right corner of the rear window
At the front and rear, or a double-sided sign on the roof
Only on the roof, facing the vehicles behind
On both front doors and on the boot lid
questions.explain: The “Learner vehicle” sign is fitted at the front and rear of motor vehicles used for driver training. On a passenger car, a double-sided sign on the roof is allowed (Basic Provisions, para. 9).

questions.q: What words are painted on the sides and rear of a training organisation's training vehicle?
options: The name of the driving school, its address and a phone number for complaints
“Caution, beginner driver” in Russian and Kazakh
None: the “Learner vehicle” sign is enough for this
“Learner vehicle” in the state language
questions.explain: In addition to the additional pedals and the identification sign, the words “Learner vehicle” in the state language are painted on the sides and rear of a training vehicle (Basic Provisions, para. 6; para. 149).

questions.q: Along which routes may driver training be conducted on public roads?
options: Along any roads except motorways and residential zones
Along routes chosen by the driving instructor
Only within 5 km of the driving school's building
Along routes agreed with the authorised body
questions.explain: Driver training on public roads is conducted only along routes agreed with the authorised body, and in the presence of a driving instructor ⟦85⟧.

questions.q: Who do the Rules treat as the driver during learner driving?
options: The driving instructor during the lesson
The director of the driving school that owns the car
Any passenger who holds a driving licence
No one: the driver is only the person holding the steering wheel
questions.explain: A driver is a person driving a vehicle, and a driving instructor is treated as the driver during the training process ⟦86⟧. That is why the requirements for a driver also apply to him.

questions.q: A driver is prohibited from handing over control to a person without a driving licence. For whom do the Rules make an exception?
options: For a close relative
For a person over 18 years old
For a person learning to drive
For someone who has passed the theory test
questions.explain: It is prohibited to hand over control to persons who do not carry a licence entitling them to drive a vehicle of that category, except for those learning to drive ⟦87⟧. But even a learner drives only under the rules of learner driving: with an instructor and without passengers ⟦88⟧.

questions.q: A driving instructor suggests that a student practise on a country road with sign 5.3 “Road for motor vehicles”. It is not marked as a motorway. May they do this?
options: Yes: learner driving is prohibited only on motorways
No: the prohibitions for motorways apply on such a road
Yes, if the route is agreed with the authorised body
Yes, if you keep to the right-hand lane
questions.explain: You are in a training vehicle (the “Learner vehicle” sign), and sign 5.3 is ahead. The requirements of the chapter on motorways also apply to roads with this sign ⟦89⟧, so learner driving is prohibited here just as on a motorway ⟦90⟧.

questions.q: The instructor wants the student to practise parking in the yard of an apartment building. There is no sign 5.38 “Residential zone” at the entrance to the yard. May learner driving be conducted here?
options: Yes: without sign 5.38, this is an ordinary road
Yes, if you drive no faster than 20 km/h
Yes, if there are no pedestrians or children in the yard
No: the rules of a residential zone apply in yards
questions.explain: The requirements of the chapter on residential zones also apply to residential courtyards, even without sign 5.38 ⟦91⟧. Learner driving is prohibited in a residential zone ⟦92⟧, so parking is practised in an enclosed area or at a test ground.

questions.q: A student with basic skills wants to drive the training vehicle to the test ground by himself, while the instructor arrives there separately. May this be done?
options: Yes, if this route is agreed with the authorised body
No: on the road, a learner drives only with the instructor
Yes, if the “Learner vehicle” sign is fitted on the car
Yes, if the student has already turned eighteen
questions.explain: Without the instructor present, a student on the road is a driver without a licence. Learner driving on the roads takes place only with an instructor ⟦93⟧ and in the presence of a driving instructor ⟦94⟧.

questions.q: May learner driving be conducted in a car with additional pedals but without the “Learner vehicle” identification sign?
options: Yes: the main thing is to have the additional pedals
Yes, during daylight hours, when the car can be seen
No: the “Learner vehicle” sign is mandatory too
Yes, if the instructor warns other drivers in advance
questions.explain: The “Learner vehicle” sign warns others that a beginner is at the wheel. A training vehicle is fitted with additional pedals and the “Learner vehicle” identification sign (para. 149; Basic Provisions, para. 6, para. 9).
